## Price spike possible

In AT, BE, CZ, DE, DK1, DK2, FR and NL there is a new binary sensor, **Price
spike possible** - the hint the Energy Price Forecast app shows since November.
It is on while the forecast marks an upcoming evening hour (16:00-23:00 local)
as a possible price spike, judged by a regional index across these markets:
high residual load, tight reserves, little wind and sun. `next_start` and
`next_end` say when; `periods` lists every marked stretch. The marked slots
also carry `spike_possible: true` in the price series' `raw_forecast`, so a
chart can colour them. The prices themselves are not changed.

**It is disabled by default, and it is often wrong** - please read this before
automating on it. Live from 18 October to 13 November, 106 of 192 marked hours
were real spikes, in a November with far more evening spikes than usual. Over
a whole year, expect about one mark in seven to come true. That makes it useful
where a false alarm costs little - keeping a home battery charged for the
evening, running a heat pump a bit ahead - and not for switching something
off. Enable it on the device page if that fits your setup. Without a fresh
index it is unavailable rather than claiming no spike is in sight.

Elsewhere the entity is not created.

## How do you use it?

If you try the new sensor - or anything else here - a line in
[Discussions](https://github.com/BackupBaTTerY/energypriceforecast-home-assistant/discussions)
on what you switch with it and whether it helped decides what comes next.
